tasks.short: Write session notes, complete assessment forms, write progress and follow-up reports, check them, send them to the referrer, and register activities for funding.

steps.what: Vision rehabilitation therapist writes notes to document training sessions: typed today; after the change spoken as a short summary that a scribe turns into a draft

loop.input: The therapist's spoken summary after the session and the client's goals in the record.
loop.output: A draft session note in the record's format.
loop.check: A validator flags any goal, aid or risk statement that does not match the record; the therapist reads the draft against what happened in the session and the spoken summary, corrects it, and types the note when the draft misses or changes a point, before it is saved.
loop.stop: One draft per session; if the therapist rejects it, they type the note.
loop.why_not_simpler: Training sessions vary; a fixed form does not capture what the client learned.

steps.what: Vision rehabilitation therapist completes assessment forms
Vision rehabilitation therapist writes progress and follow-up outcome reports

loop.input: The session notes, assessment results and goals in the record.
loop.output: A draft progress or follow-up report.
loop.check: Code checks every goal, score and aid named in the draft against the record and flags mismatches; the therapist reads each statement against the session notes and assessments, including their limits, and rewrites what the record does not support.
loop.stop: One draft per report; if the therapist rejects it, they write the report.
loop.why_not_simpler: Referrers want a short narrative of progress; a list of scores does not give it.

steps.what: Vision rehabilitation therapist checks the final report: progress, scores and advice match the record and its limits, and the addressee is the referrer
Vision rehabilitation therapist sends the checked report to the referrer: by e-mail today, by one release through the secure care exchange after the change

Vision rehabilitation therapist registers activities for funding: by hand today; after the change codes follow from the appointment type by fixed rules and the therapist checks them against the sessions held

tasks.design: After a session, the therapist speaks a short summary and a scribe drafts the note; a validator flags goals, aids and risk statements that do not match the record, and the therapist approves before saving. Assessment forms are filled on a tablet in the record ({OTHER}); this first record keeps its time. Progress and follow-up reports are drafted from the record and checked against it; the therapist checks each report and releases it to the referrer through the secure care exchange. Funding codes follow from the appointment type by fixed rules. Sessions are not recorded.
tasks.previous_blocker: Notes, forms and reports were typed after each session.
tasks.enabler_now: Scribes draft notes the clinician validates; records derive codes from appointments.
tasks.still_hard: Many sessions happen outdoors, away from a screen.
tasks.human_edge: Describing what a client can now do safely on their own.
tasks.altitude: The therapist validates drafts instead of typing.

evidence.claim: Autoscriber drafts the note and the clinician validates it before it goes into the record.
At Capio Ramsay Santé, 1,295 clinicians reported time per note falling from 6.69 to 4.72 minutes with Tandem notes; three of seven authors were from the vendor.
Recording captures staff performance and needs works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the session held to activities registered; funder processing is outside.
Input contract: goals and assessments in the record; fallback is typing.
The therapist approves every note and report.
A DPIA and works council consent come before use.

s1 keeps 80: speaking a summary is quicker than typing, but the note is the therapist's own record and every draft is read. s2 is a first record and keeps its full time. s3 keeps 70 because each report is read against the record. s5 keeps 10 for the release; s6 keeps 30 for checking codes.
research_questions: How long does the therapist spend editing drafts?

already_counted.description: Vision rehabilitation therapist edits drafted notes.
Vision rehabilitation therapist edits drafted reports.

incremental.description: No new work: speaking the summary replaces typing and is inside s1.

approvals.approved_version: The progress or follow-up report exactly as checked by the therapist in s4, sent once to the named referrer through the secure care exchange; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: drafts from short summaries and the record need heavy edits, so s1 keeps 90 and s3 keeps 85 (15.2); high: drafts as designed (22.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Train clients to use touch, hearing, movement, smell and body sense, note exercises and progress, and plan the next exercises.

steps.what: Vision rehabilitation therapist trains clients to use tactile, auditory, kinesthetic, olfactory and proprioceptive information
Vision rehabilitation therapist notes exercises and progress in free text
Vision rehabilitation therapist plans the next exercises

tasks.design: Exercises are ticked from a standard exercise list per sense in the record ({OTHER}) with a short progress score, instead of free-text notes. Training clients and planning the next exercises stay with the therapist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Progress was described in free text after each session.
tasks.enabler_now: Records can hold exercise lists with progress scores.
tasks.still_hard: Progress in sensory skills is gradual and hard to score.
tasks.human_edge: Guiding a client's hand to feel the edge of a kerb.

reach.learn: Whether home practice matches the sessions.

evidence.claim: Records can hold standard exercise lists with progress scores.

assumptions: Boundary: from the training plan to the next exercises; aids supply is outside.
Input contract: exercise list agreed in the team; fallback is free text.
Training does not change.
Clients' time does not change.
s2 keeps 80: ticking exercises from a list saves some typing, but the progress note is the therapist's own first record.
research_questions: Is progress easier to follow across therapists?

incremental.description: Vision rehabilitation therapist keeps the exercise list current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the standard list fits few of the exercises used, so free text stays and s2 keeps 95 (0.0); high: most exercises are on the list (1.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read the referral and eye reports, assess the client's vision, mobility, cognition and emotional functioning, discuss personal goals, and record the assessment.

steps.what: Vision rehabilitation therapist reads the referral and eye reports: paper letters scanned into the record today, arriving through the secure care exchange after the change
Vision rehabilitation therapist assesses clients' functioning in vision, orientation and mobility, cognition and physical abilities
Vision rehabilitation therapist discusses social and emotional issues and personal goals
Vision rehabilitation therapist records the assessment from handwritten notes

tasks.design: Referrals and eye reports arrive in the record ({OTHER}) through the secure care exchange instead of as letters. The assessment is filled on a tablet form with standard items per area during the visit, so it is not typed from handwritten notes. Assessing the client and discussing goals stay with the therapist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Referral letters were read on paper and assessments typed from notes.
tasks.enabler_now: Care exchanges carry referrals; tablet forms fill the record.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing the fear behind a client's wish to stay indoors.

evidence.claim: Secure care exchanges can carry referrals; tablet forms can fill the record.
The dossier is kept twenty years after the last change.

assumptions: Boundary: from the referral to the assessment recorded; the training plan is outside.
Input contract: referrers use the secure exchange; fallback is paper letters.
Assessing and discussing do not change.
Clients' time does not change.

s1 keeps 80: reading stays; scanning and filing letters goes. s4 keeps 50 for free-text parts of the assessment; typing from handwritten notes goes. Filling the tablet form during the visit takes about the time notes took, so s2 and s3 keep 100.
research_questions: Are assessments in the record sooner?

incremental.description: Vision rehabilitation therapist scans paper referrals that still arrive.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: most referrers keep sending paper letters, so s1 keeps 100, and many notes stay handwritten, so s4 keeps 70 (4.0); high: referrals through the exchange and the tablet form used as designed (10.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare route descriptions and tactile maps, teach clients to travel independently on real routes, run simulated travel exercises, and note progress.

steps.what: Vision rehabilitation therapist prepares route descriptions and tactile maps by hand
Vision rehabilitation therapist teaches clients to travel independently on actual routes
Vision rehabilitation therapist runs simulated travel situations and exercises
Vision rehabilitation therapist notes travel progress

tasks.design: Tactile route maps are produced from digital map data and printed on swell paper, and route descriptions start from a template with landmarks per route, so the therapist adapts them instead of drawing by hand. Progress per route segment is ticked in the record ({OTHER}); this first record keeps most of its time. Teaching on real routes and in simulated situations stays with the therapist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Tactile maps and route descriptions were made by hand for each client.
tasks.enabler_now: Map data can be turned into tactile prints on swell paper.
tasks.human_edge: Judging when a client is ready to cross a busy street alone.

reach.learn: Whether they use new routes sooner.

evidence.claim: Map data can be turned into tactile maps printed on swell paper.

assumptions: Boundary: from the client route to progress noted; aids supply is outside.
Input contract: open map data for the area; fallback is drawing by hand.
Teaching travel does not change.
Clients' time does not change.
s1 keeps 50 for adapting each map and description to the client. s4 keeps 85: ticking segments saves some typing, but the progress note is the therapist's own record.
research_questions: Do clients learn routes in fewer sessions?

incremental.description: Vision rehabilitation therapist checks generated maps against the real route.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: map data lack the detail clients need, so most maps are still drawn by hand and s1 keeps 80 (2.2); high: open map data cover the routes (5.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The vision rehabilitation therapist keeps assessing, training senses and teaching travel; typed notes, hand-drawn maps and paper referrals shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A therapist with more time outdoors with clients.

job.title: Low Vision Therapists, Orientation and Mobility Specialists, and Vision Rehabilitation Therapists
